questions.question: What are the basic components of a graph?
questions.explanation: The basic components of a graph are nodes and edges. Nodes represent entities and edges represent the relationships between these entities.

questions.question: In graph theory, what do nodes typically represent?
questions.explanation: In graph theory, nodes typically represent entities, such as people, locations, websites, or any other objects that can have relationships with one another.

questions.question: In a social network, what do edges typically represent?
questions.explanation: In a social network, edges typically represent relationships between entities, such as friendship connections, follower relationships, or interactions between users.

questions.question: What is another common name for a node in a graph?
questions.explanation: Another common name for a node is a vertex. Both terms refer to the same concept in graph theory - an entity in the graph.

questions.question: What is another common name for an edge in a social network?
questions.explanation: Another common name for an edge in a social network is a tie. This term is often used in social network analysis to represent relationships or connections between actors.

questions.question: What are edges in a directed graph called?
questions.explanation: Edges in a directed graph are called arcs. An arc has a direction, indicating that the relationship goes from one node to another but not necessarily in the reverse direction.

questions.question: In an undirected graph, an edge indicates that the relationship between nodes is?
questions.explanation: In an undirected graph, an edge indicates that the relationship between nodes is mutual, meaning it goes both ways. There is no direction associated with the relationship.

questions.question: A graph with weighted edges is called what?
questions.explanation: A graph where edges have weights (values associated with them) is called a weighted graph. These weights can represent distances, costs, or strengths of relationships.

questions.question: What is the size of a graph typically measured by?
options: The sum of nodes and edges
questions.explanation: The size of a graph is typically measured by the number of nodes it contains. This is denoted as |V| in mathematical notation.

questions.question: The length of the shortest path between two nodes is called?
questions.explanation: The length of the shortest path between two nodes is called the distance between those nodes. It represents the minimum number of edges that must be traversed to go from one node to the other.

questions.question: The length of the longest shortest path between any pair of nodes in a graph is called?
questions.explanation: The diameter of a graph is the length of the longest shortest path between any pair of nodes. It represents the maximum distance between any two nodes in the graph.

questions.question: An edge whose removal increases the number of connected components in a graph is called a?
questions.explanation: An edge whose removal increases the number of connected components in a graph is called a bridge. Bridges are critical connections that, if removed, would disconnect parts of the graph.

questions.question: In an undirected graph, the number of edges connected to a node is called the node's?
questions.explanation: In an undirected graph, the number of edges connected to a node is called the node's degree. This is a basic measure of how connected a node is within the graph.

questions.question: In a directed graph, the number of edges pointing towards a node is called the node's?
questions.explanation: In a directed graph, the number of edges pointing towards a node is called the node's in-degree. It represents how many other nodes have connections directed at this node.

questions.question: In a directed graph, the number of edges pointing away from a node is called the node's?
questions.explanation: In a directed graph, the number of edges pointing away from a node is called the node's out-degree. It represents how many connections the node directs toward other nodes.

questions.question: An undirected graph with no cycles and exactly one path between any two nodes is called a?
questions.explanation: An undirected graph with no cycles and exactly one path between any two nodes is called a tree. Trees are connected acyclic graphs that have n-1 edges for n nodes.

questions.question: A graph in which all possible edges exist is called a?
questions.explanation: A graph in which all possible edges exist is called a complete graph. In a complete graph with n nodes, every node is connected to every other node, resulting in n(n-1)/2 edges.

questions.question: A graph whose nodes can be divided into two disjoint sets such that every edge connects a node in one set to one in the other is called a?
questions.explanation: A graph whose nodes can be divided into two disjoint sets such that every edge connects a node in one set to one in the other is called a bipartite graph. Examples include user-item networks in recommendation systems.

questions.question: Which of the following is a way to represent a graph?
questions.explanation: An adjacency matrix is a common way to represent a graph. It's an n×n matrix where n is the number of nodes, and each cell (i,j) indicates whether there is an edge between nodes i and j.

questions.question: In an adjacency matrix, if there is an edge between node i and node j, the corresponding element in the matrix is typically?
questions.explanation: In an adjacency matrix, if there is an edge between node i and node j, the corresponding element (i,j) in the matrix is typically 1. If there is no edge, the value is 0.

questions.question: The adjacency matrices of social media networks are usually?
questions.explanation: The adjacency matrices of social media networks are usually sparse, meaning most elements are zero. This is because most users are connected to only a small fraction of all users in the network.

questions.question: A graph representation that maintains a list of all the nodes that each node is connected to is called a(n)?
questions.explanation: A graph representation that maintains a list of all the nodes that each node is connected to is called an adjacency list. For each node, it stores a list of its neighboring nodes.

questions.question: A graph representation in which each element is an edge and is usually represented as a pair of connected nodes is called a(n)?
questions.explanation: A graph representation in which each element is an edge and is usually represented as a pair of connected nodes is called an edge list. It simply lists all the edges in the graph as pairs of nodes.

questions.question: In social network analysis, the network focused on a focal actor (ego) and a set of alters who have ties with the ego is called a(n)?
questions.explanation: In social network analysis, the network focused on a focal actor (ego) and a set of alters who have ties with the ego is called an egocentric network. It examines the local network structure around a specific individual.

questions.question: A graph in which all nodes have the same degree is called a?
questions.explanation: A graph in which all nodes have the same degree is called a regular graph. If each node has degree k, it's called a k-regular graph.
